body:
You can easily achieve the same result using `ease-in-out`, thus avoiding the warning in console.

```javascript
  animations: [
    trigger('toolbarAnimations', [
      state('void, leave', style({ transform: 'translateY(-100%)' })),
      state('enter', style({ transform: 'none' })),
      transition(':enter', [
        sequence([
          animate('200ms ease-in-out', style({ transform: 'none' })),
          animate('200ms ease-in-out', style({ transform: 'translateY(-12px)' })),
          animate('250ms ease-in-out', style({ transform: 'none' })),
        ]),
      ]),
      transition(':leave', group([animate('300ms ease-in-out', style({ transform: 'translateY(-100%)' }))])),
    ])
```

This would avoid the warning (workaround the bug), but it will also change the animated result. We are aiming for a bounce effect that isn't achieved by using `ease-in-out `in all animations.
 
See https://stackoverflow.com/questions/9629346/difference-between-css3-transitions-ease-in-and-ease-out#9636239 to see why the ease-in-out will give a different effect.

@noudenaa I've implemented the non-animatable warnings some time ago, sorry I must have missed the timing functions, I'll look at this very soon 🙂 

In the meantime, I hope that this is not blocking you? if I'm not mistaken the non-animatable warnings don't show up in production so this should hopefully just be an inconvenience during dev time?
Thanks. It is not blocking, the warnings indeed don't show up in production.

body:
Hi @xunillinux I don't think you are doing anything wrong, the issue is that the check to see if a property is animatable has been implemented following this set of properties: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_animated_properties

The issue is that your property is an animatable svg one which happens to be also acceptable as css, thus it is not included in the list.

I checked and various other svg attributes would cause the same problem: https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG/propidx.html

The easiest solution for your problem would be to add all of those here: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/3a60063a54d850c50ce962a8a39ce01cfee71398/packages/animations/browser/src/render/web_animations/animatable_props_set.ts#L14
but in order to do that I think we may want to have a definitive source (like the one we have for the css animatable props) (the one I linked above does say that it is just informative, so I am not sure if that's reliable enough)

The alternative would be to allow the developer to specify somewhere the properties they do not want non-animatable warnings for (no, there isn't currently a way to do so :sweat:), this would also make the warning more configurable. (I think this might be preferred if not many people animate svgs, if svg animation via angular animations is common then maybe we should focus on adding the svg properties instead).

What do you think? Which from your perspective sounds like the way to go?

Hey @dario-piotrowicz Thank you for your answer.
Okay I don't know how many people use svg animatable properties but I don't think I'm the only one. So maybe it would be good to add those to the list. But nevertheless I think a configuration option for disabling the warning for specific cases might be a good solution. There may be some other usecases where there is an unnecessary warning or maybe some people would choose to ignore the warning on purpose.

Cool, I can see that my PR for this current issue is getting merged soon 🙂, after that I'll look into adding the svg props and/or adding an option to disable warnings 🙂👍 

@xunillinux if you want please feel free to open an issue and tag me there, otherwise I guess I can just do it without an issue to back it up, whatever you prefer (if you create the issue I'll be easier to keep track of it and you can get notified there 🙂)
